gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Apple rates the M2 Pro to M4 Max MacBook Pros for 4K above 60 Hz only on their HDMI port, with Thunderbolt listed at 6K 60 Hz. The same results also don't state that every DP 1.4 '4K144' claim needs DSC because 4K144 at 8-bit RGB carries 28.67 Gb/s of active pixels against DP 1.4's 25.92 Gb/s payload. Together these favour an HDMI 2.1 KVM over the USB-C-to-DisplayPort route ChatGPT and Level1Techs suggest.
standout_why: I compared against these pages: the TESmart HDMI 2.1 gaming guide (cited) and the TESmart DSC blog (cited), which say 4K144 'often depends on timing and color settings', give no Gb/s figure for 4K144 and tell Mac buyers to 'confirm the external-display limits of the exact Mac model'. The Level1Techs KVM FAQ (cited) already says DP 1.4 4K144 works only with DSC ('Without DSC, no') and recommends a USB-C-to-DP cable for Macs, so that half is partly covered. The Level1Techs single-monitor store page (cited) lists 4K120 only. The TESmart DKS202-MC24 and HKS202-M24 pages (cited) were rate-limited for page reads, but the store data shows the problem below. None of these pages gives Apple's per-port refresh limits for each chip, Apple's note that adapters aren't supported at 4K240 over HDMI, the fact that the 2021 M1 Pro/Max HDMI port tops out at 4K60, or that TESmart's own resolution list for the 'Dual 4K144Hz' HKS202-M24 contains no 4K144 mode.
decides: The pick now depends on which Mac the shopper has. With an M2 Pro, M3 Pro or M4 Pro/Max MacBook Pro, the only port Apple rates for 4K above 60 Hz is HDMI. So an HDMI 2.1 KVM whose maker lists a 4K high-refresh mode is the sourced path: the TESmart HDK202-M24 lists 'Dual 4K@144Hz/160Hz (DSC 1.2a)', and the HKS201-M24 lists 4K240 (DSC). A DP 1.4 KVM fed by USB-C-to-DP (Level1Techs, TESmart DKS202-M24) has no Apple 4K144 rating on those Macs and needs DSC at 4K144 in any case. With a 2021 M1 Pro/Max, an HDMI KVM caps the Mac at 4K60. M5 Pro/Max is rated for 4K144 over Thunderbolt or HDMI, so either KVM type is possible. The current page's 'use the monitor's KVM' advice still holds, because a direct HDMI cable avoids the middle device, and Apple says to 'Connect displays directly to your Mac for best results'.

findings.label: DP 1.4 (HBR3) usable video payload
findings.value: 25.92 Gb/s (32.4 Gb/s raw over four lanes)
findings.source_title: VESA Rolls Out Early Certification Program for Video Source and Display Products Using HBR3 High-Bandwidth Link Rate
findings.note: VESA: 'combined audio/video payload data rate of 25.92 Gbps'. Arithmetic for 4K144 at 8-bit RGB, active pixels only: 3840×2160×144×24 bit = 28.67 Gb/s, which exceeds 25.92 before any blanking is added. 4K120 gives 23.89 Gb/s, which fits. At 10-bit, 4K144 needs 35.83 Gb/s. So a DP 1.4 KVM's '4K144' always means DSC (or chroma subsampling), whatever the label says.
